title.narrative: BRIDGE: Bridging Communities to Protect Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms

description.narrative:
Overall Objective: To create a conducive environment in which human rights and fundamental freedoms, of women, youth and marginalized communities, are respected and protected.

Specific Objective: To enable and empower 200 women and youth (CSO and political) leaders, and 100 Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) and build solidarity amongst 15 people¿s forums to promote peaceful, inclusive, and resilient communities in

5 districts in Northern Sri Lanka.

Outcome 1: To enhance support and deepen engagement with 200 women and youth leaders and 100 HRDs to facilitate and lead political and economic transformation and challenge the structural constraints that exclude women and youth.

Outcome 2: To promote collective action and solidarity, improve access to legal and other support services for women and youth leaders and HRDs and promote awareness and appreciation of human rights including gender equality through digital innovation and responsible social media access and use.

title.narrative: 1.2.2: Number of reforms and specific measures taken to advocate at various level to promote womens political participation.

description.narrative: The indicator will measure the number of reforms or measures issued through Government, Gazette or through other valid documentation available online, published in hard copies or shared as a soft copy. Reforms or measures can be a new provision or extension of an existing provision made to promote womens political participation at the national, local level. Provision refers to statute, law, ordinance, rule, regulation.concerning any of the following Provincial, Municipal, Urban councils, Pradeshya Sabha, Cooperatives, Rural Development Societies, Community Centers etc.

comment.narrative: During baseline assessment participants cited the 25 quota system for women contestants as the only reform or specific measure that has been taken.
At least 3 measures in the form of reform or policy recommendations are presented in local and national level to promote womens political participation.

title.narrative: Proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments and (b) local governments

description.narrative: SDG indicator 5.5.1 under (a) measures the proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments, currently as at 1 January of reporting year, is currently measured as the number of seats held by women members in single or lower chambers of national parliaments, expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. National parliaments can be bicameral or unicameral. This indicator covers the single chamber in unicameral parliaments and the lower chamber in bicameral parliaments. It does not cover the upper chamber of bicameral parliaments. Seats are usually won by members in general parliamentary elections. Seats may also be filled by nomination, appointment, indirect election, rotation of members and byelection. Seats refer to the number of parliamentary mandates, or the number of members of parliament.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. Users are not expected to encode values for these indicators.For more detailed information, see https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/

comment.narrative: Following the 2018 election for local authorities there were 173 elected female members out of 761 total members in local authorities.
5 increase in the national parliament

description.narrative: SDG indicator 5.5.1 under (a) measures the proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments, currently as at 1 January of reporting year, is currently measured as the number of seats held by women members in single or lower chambers of national parliaments, expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. National parliaments can be bicameral or unicameral. This indicator covers the single chamber in unicameral parliaments and the lower chamber in bicameral parliaments. It does not cover the upper chamber of bicameral parliaments. Seats are usually won by members in general parliamentary elections. Seats may also be filled by nomination, appointment, indirect election, rotation of members and byelection. Seats refer to the number of parliamentary mandates, or the number of members of parliament.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. Users are not expected to encode values for these indicators.For more detailed information, see https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/
